samples.text:
Nowadays many young people have problem to save money, even when they have a job. This essay will explain the reasons for this and suggest some ways to encourage them to save more.

There are several reasons why young people find it difficult to save. Firstly, the cost of living is very high today, especially in big cities. Rent, transport and food are expensive, so after paying all the bills, there is not much money left. Secondly, young people are influenced by social media and advertising. They see their friends or influencers buying new clothes, phones and going on holidays, and they want to do the same. Also, online shopping and credit cards make spending very easy, because you can buy something with one click and pay later. Another reason is that many young people did not learn how to manage money at school or at home.

There are some ways to encourage young people to save. Firstly, schools should teach financial education, for example how to make a budget and why saving is important. If students learn this early, they will have good habits in the future. Secondly, banks can offer special saving accounts for young people with higher interest, so saving becomes more attractive. There are also mobile apps which can save small amount of money automatically every time you spend. Finally, parents should give a good example and talk with their children about money.

In conclusion, young people find it hard to save because of high living costs, social pressure and easy spending. Financial education, special accounts and apps can help them to save more money for the future.
samples.why: Both questions answered with relevant causes and suggestions · limited development of each idea · formulaic linking (Firstly, Secondly, Also) · some collocation errors · article and structure errors that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
Many young adults today struggle to put money aside, even when they are in full-time employment. This essay will examine the main reasons for this difficulty and suggest measures that could encourage younger people to develop better saving habits.

The most significant factor is the high cost of living. In many cities, rents have risen much faster than wages, so a large proportion of a young person's income is spent on accommodation before other essential expenses such as transport and food are even considered. For those who are also repaying student loans, the money available for saving is even smaller. Consumer culture adds to the problem. Social media constantly exposes young people to images of fashionable products, restaurants and holidays, creating pressure to keep up with their peers. At the same time, contactless payments and 'buy now, pay later' services make spending so effortless that many people lose track of how much they have spent. Finally, a lack of financial education means that many young adults have never been taught how to budget effectively.

Several steps could help to change this situation. Schools could make personal finance a compulsory part of the curriculum, teaching students how to plan a budget, understand interest and avoid unnecessary debt. Banks and technology companies also have a role to play; apps that automatically round up purchases and transfer the difference into a savings account make saving almost effortless. Governments could offer incentives, such as tax-free savings accounts or bonuses for young people saving towards their first home, which would give them a clear goal to work towards. In addition, clearer regulation of short-term credit would reduce the temptation to overspend.

In conclusion, young people find saving difficult because of high living costs, social pressure and easy access to credit. Financial education, smart technology and government incentives could encourage them to builds more secure financial futures.
samples.why: Both questions answered clearly with extended, relevant support · logical organisation and good cohesion · less common vocabulary used appropriately (put money aside, incentives, overspend) · mostly error-free with one verb-form slip.

samples.text:
For many young adults, building up savings now feels like an unattainable goal. The explanation lies partly in economic conditions beyond their control and partly in a consumer environment that makes spending effortless, but there are practical ways in which saving could be made both easier and more appealing.

Structural pressures are the most obvious obstacle. Housing costs in many cities have far outpaced wages, so rent alone can absorb a substantial share of a young worker's income, and entry-level jobs are increasingly insecure or poorly paid. Loan repayments for education leave even less room for anything else. These constraints are compounded by the culture in which young people live. Social media presents a constant stream of holidays, restaurants and new products, making modest living feel like missing out, while frictionless digital payments and instalment schemes disguise the true cost of purchases. Furthermore, many young adults leave school without ever having been taught to budget, so even those with some spare income may lack the habits needed to retain it.

Encouraging saving therefore requires a combination of education, design and incentives. Personal finance should be taught in schools as a practical skill, covering budgeting, interest and the dangers of high-cost credit, so that good habits are formed before the first salary arrives. Financial technology can also be harnessed for positive ends: automatic transfers on payday and apps that round up transactions into savings make putting money aside the default rather than an act of willpower. Governments could strengthen motivation by offering bonuses or tax advantages on savings for specific goals, such as a first home, and tighter regulation of instalment schemes would make the cost of borrowing more transparent.

In conclusion, young people struggle to save because of high living costs, insecure work and a culture that encourages consumption. By teaching financial skills early, designing tools that make saving automatic and offering meaningful incentives, society could help them build greater financial security.
samples.why: Both questions fully answered with perceptive, well-developed ideas · skilful sequencing from causes to matching solutions · precise, natural vocabulary (outpaced, frictionless, harnessed) · wide range of accurate complex structures.
